title: This Portfolio
summary: This site: one data layer driving a homepage, four role-specific portfolios and project case studies, with static meta tags generated for each route at build time.

caseStudy.overview: A recruiter-focused portfolio where each career path has its own URL that makes sense on its own.
caseStudy.problem: Mobile engineering, product design and program leadership read as three unrelated CVs when they're listed side by side. Recruiters need the one view that matches their role.
contribution: Content model in plain JS modules: experience, projects, roles and credentials.
One role-page template driven by data, so each path has a focused page without duplicate components.
A post-build script that writes per-route HTML with its own title, description, canonical URL and Open Graph tags, plus sitemap.xml and robots.txt.
constraints: Static hosting on GitHub Pages — no server rendering.
No new dependencies beyond the existing React/Vite stack.
caseStudy.approach: Content first: every page reads from the same data files, so adding a project or a role-specific CV is a data change, not a layout change.

decisions.title: Static HTML per route instead of a prerender framework
decisions.body: Link previews on LinkedIn and Slack don't run JavaScript. Writing a small HTML file per route with the right meta tags fixes that without adding SSR tooling.

decisions.title: Hide gaps instead of filling them
decisions.body: Case-study fields without real content are omitted in production and flagged in development, so nothing on the site is invented to look complete.

outcomes: Live on GitHub Pages, with a shareable URL per career path.
